findings.summary: Ship s-9001 was rewritten ~3h after creation in violation of Requirement 4.4 10-minute edit rule. Root cause was ChronoUnit.HOURS instead of MINUTES creating a 10-hour window. CI stayed green because the asserting ShipServiceTest is excluded from MVP_TESTS and ShipControllerTest mocks the service. Patch to MINUTES fixes expiry and makes the covering test pass.

second_opinion.summary: Patch changes ChronoUnit.HOURS to MINUTES on the editWindowExpires calculation, directly fixing the 10-hour window that allowed 3h-late edits in s-9001/s-9017. Enforcement logic in Ship.isEditWindowOpen was already correct; only expiry was wrong, now fixed and previously failing ShipServiceTest passes with no regressions.

hypotheses.note: Line 76 with HOURS plus 3h successful updates directly imply 600-min window; isEditWindowOpen exists but uses wrong expiry, so claim follows.
CI MVP_TESTS excludes ShipServiceTest and ShipControllerTest mocks ShipService; excluded test demonstrates it would have caught bug (expected 10 vs 600).

risks: CI still excludes ShipServiceTest in MVP_TESTS, so future regression would stay green despite correct fix
Existing persisted ships created before fix keep 10-hour editWindowExpires in DB — no migration/backfill considered
No search/fix for similar ChronoUnit misuse outside ShipService.java; Instant.now without Clock injection leaves tests flaky
